# An ordinary goal-directed baseline defeats the previous sufficient ledger

This is a **separate comparator**, not a replacement theorem or a new learning
algorithm. All earlier reviewed sources and archives remain unchanged. The
current finite-state example does not establish a consequential advantage of
our operator certificate. This comparator is goal-specific; it does not replace
the earlier uniform compatible-goal/operator certificate.

## 1. Task and actual information interface

The fixed public task is the pinned 4096-state, two-action, 24-step source,
initially uniform on its public initial support, with terminal reward the public
indicator b of G. Initial support is disjoint from G. Source access returns
sampled destination labels for named current labels/actions; block membership
is an acquired retained lookup. The learner is not given hidden groups, edge
lists, a useful decomposition, transition probabilities, or optimal values.
The same ordinary coarse-count community proposal acquires four blocks. All
pilot and incoming row-count batches used below were taken after that proposal.
The reused counts are exact recorded integers, not new observations. Direct
source implementation access appears only in the **source-side adapter audit**,
not in the planner or hazard estimator.

The deployed policy is an ordinary 24-by-4 action table with a 4096-entry block
lookup. It can run in an explicit-state simulator that returns the next label;
there is no claim of a physical sensor or hidden-state implementation. Each
step costs a source transition, label update, block lookup and policy lookup.

## 2. Confidence radius and fixed prefixes

For N iid Bernoulli trials and count c, put

    v(c)=c(N-c)/(N(N-1)),
    R(c,N,K)=min(1, sqrt_up(2 v(c) K/N) + 7K/[3(N-1)]).

`sqrt_up` is the retained exact dyadic upper square root with 40 fractional bits.
Maurer–Pontil (2009), Theorem 4, implies the one-sided upper/lower bounds at
failure probability zeta whenever K >= log(2/zeta). For two-sided receiving use
K >= log(4/zeta). We use K=(7/10) ceil(log2 x) >= ln x; ln 2 < 7/10 follows,
for example, from the positive Taylor lower sum for exp(7/10)>2.

trace stops after the third. At prefix t the row half-batch size is 512*2^t,

No correctness of the heuristic is assumed: the fixed partition is validated
on fresh observations. The initial law is explicitly uniform within blocks.
Let Z lift block functions, W average uniformly within each acquired block,

nonanticipating validation schedule are external premises, not file assertions.

 U = n/[N(N-1)] * [sum_i(C_i^2-C_i)

# Historical missing metadata and prospective exact joint retention

The historical `RoutingSource.pooled_batch` does **not** retain source-row
identities. It integrates the uniform source row into a single destination
marginal and samples only pooled destination counts. No historical row tags
can be reconstructed from that file, and none are invented here.

The real named-row interface permits the learner to choose the row and observe
the destination label. A prospective method therefore receives BOTH the pooled
microscopic destination counts and source-row -> destination-BLOCK counts with
O(nr) extra streaming counters and no extra forward call. Ordinary competitors
receive the same metadata. This changes prospective acquisition comparisons;
old sufficient ledgers were never lower bounds.

`joint_source.py` generates new joint sufficient statistics, not independently
sampled marginals. First it draws all uniform source-row choices (counts N_i)
independently of outcomes. For each row it draws mixture-branch counts. Local
neighbor counts are generated jointly as a degree-sized multinomial and added
to both retained statistics; deterministic global-branch destinations likewise
update both. Macro and reset destinations are **actually sampled individually**
and their same labels update both statistics. Conditional on source/branch
counts this is exactly the same joint law as repeated ordinary transitions;
summing over those counts proves the unconditional iid pooled law. Cross-table
block totals are checked exactly. Aggregate simulation saves time, not logical
source calls. The number of actually generated macro/reset destination labels,
row multinomials, counter work, retained bytes and elapsed time must be charged.

The prototype uses power-of-two source blocks and local degree. Its first three
branch probabilities are exactly the binary64 argument values used by the
original `_row_counts`; the fourth is the remaining rational mass. Uniform
within-row groups and neighbor slots are generated by integer indices or exact
dyadic multinomial arguments. Thus its ideal argument-law model is the original
ordinary `_row_counts` law, not a silent conversion of the old separately
normalized `row_block_batch` / `pooled_batch` laws. Old column/coarse data used
that ordinary branch law and can still serve as previously paid discovery/
